title: Service & Business Logic Architecture
outcome: Move orchestration and business invariants into cohesive services/policies so transport and persistence details do not become the domain model.
artifact: Refactored task service with explicit policies/invariants and thin controllers.
labSteps: Choose one endpoint with mixed concerns and list every responsibility it currently performs.
Move HTTP-only concerns back to controller/boundary and persistence mechanics behind a focused collaborator.
Express one business rule with a name that describes the rule, not the framework.
Add a use-case method whose inputs/outputs make orchestration visible.
Test the rule without booting the whole web server where practical.
Review the resulting dependency direction and remove abstractions that add no clarity.
failureModes: God services with hundreds of unrelated lines
Business rules duplicated in controllers and frontend
Repository abstraction added before there is a boundary to protect
Methods named only after CRUD verbs when workflow intent matters
mastery: Can place a rule in the correct layer
Can refactor without changing external behavior
principles: Business rules belong in services or domain-focused collaborators, not duplicated across controllers and components.
Keep orchestration separate from low-level persistence details so behavior can be tested clearly.
Make rule boundaries explicit before adding abstractions such as repositories.
Prefer small cohesive methods that communicate intent over giant service methods that mix validation, authorization, and I/O.
